transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Avery, Riley (Redwood); Clara, Marcus, Samir (Nimbus)
Shared artifacts: Deck: https://redwood.example.com/decks/capacity-tether; Security pack: https://redwood.example.com/sec/nimbus-soc2; Benchmark sheet: https://sheets.example.com/bench-93921

Summary:
Quick renewal+expansion check-in; customer wants a predictable burst band across APAC and EU for peak holiday weekend traffic, discuss dedicated vs reserved burst capacity, SLAs, VPC/onprem pilot timeline, and contract amendment language.

Topics covered:
- Current consumption & seasonal spike profile
- Dedicated vs hosted burst economics
- Private (VPC/on-prem) pilot logistics and KMS/encryption concerns
- Latency SLOs and fallback behavior
- Contract amendment and timing

Action items (captured in metadata above).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for making time. um quick check — is this still the right agenda? renewal, burst capacity, onprem pilot?
[00:08] Clara Gomez: yep that's right; Marcus will speak to product needs but i'm mostly here for ops and timelines.
[00:12] Marcus Lee: yeah hi all, we've got a big promotion in june that doubles inference traffic in apac for two 72-hour windows, so need a plan that doesn't break the backend or blow the budget.
[00:23] Riley Patel: got it. Riley from Redwood infra. quick question on current numbers — Clara you mentioned 300 rps average, what's peak now in EU and APAC?
[00:31] Clara Gomez: currently peak eu we see 2.4k rps, apac is smaller today ~800 but expected to hit 5k during promos. our KV cache hit is... maybe 25% right now, we can tune prompts but not a lot of headroom.
[00:44] Riley Patel: okay, that helps. on Redwood side we can do two approaches: reserved capacity (dedicated pools) with burst lanes or a temporary dedicated burst addendum that layers onto your hosted tier. ded is more predictable for latency; hosted burst cheaper but less isolation.
[01:02] Samir Rao: latency is the big ask — p95 needs to stay <120ms for completion tokens during peak, or some flows time out. also we need egress and encryption constraints: all customer data must not leave eu/apac the region (data residency).
[01:17] Avery Chen: noted. we have private deployment options for sovereignty — vpc + private control plane — and an onprem package if you need fully air-gapped. Would you be looking at full onprem or VPC-only?
[01:27] Marcus Lee: VPC should be fine for now, but we might require a short onprem pilot to validate throughput with our firewall stack.
[01:34] Clara Gomez: and, can you confirm KMS/HSM options? we need SSE with our key custody; can't have tokens with Redwood-managed keys for certain flows.
[01:43] Riley Patel: yes, our private deploy supports customer-managed KMS (we've done AWS KMS and an HSM integration for a few customers). there are a couple of limitations documented in the security pack — we'll share that.
[01:52] Marcus Lee: great. about the burst model, what's the minimum lead time to spin up APAC nodes and guarantee capacity?
[01:58] Avery Chen: for reserved capacity we typically need 2-3 weeks to provision and validate; for a burst addendum we can enable a soft-burst within 48-72 hours but without full SLA for latency. If you need guaranteed p95 targets we'd recommend dedicated pool in apac provisioned ahead of time.
[02:16] Samir Rao: hmm 2-3 weeks is okay but the promotion is mid-June so we need the contract and provisioning locked by end of April. Can we align on the contract amendment by then?
[02:26] Avery Chen: yes that's doable. we'll draft an amendment that includes APAC burst band + EU buffer and an enrollment clause for onprem pilot.
[02:33] Riley Patel: from a technical perspective, we recommend enabling prefix KV caching and quantization profile Q4 for your models — that typically reduces tokens/cost and keeps latency under target. however quantization has some regen quality delta; Marcus, will product accept a small quality delta?
[02:48] Marcus Lee: we'd prefer no regression in customer-facing summary generation. but for internal A/B flows maybe okay. we need to see evals.
[02:55] Riley Patel: okay we'll run a quick eval set and share results. we'll also include a suggestion for batching thresholds — don't want to increase tail latency.
[03:03] Clara Gomez: on monitoring — can we get token-level cost and latency breakdowns by route? our finance team needs that for the promo.
[03:10] Avery Chen: yes the Redwood console has per-route dashboards. we can also enable extended retention for the promo window (extra fee).
[03:18] Samir Rao: what about fallback behavior if dedicated pool hits capacity? we need a policy for graceful degradation — prefer fallback to a cheaper model variant in-region rather than cross-region routing.
[03:27] Riley Patel: we can set routing policy to prefer same-region, then fallback to a smaller quantized model variant with explicit rewrite. auto-fallback to another region is only for critical paths and can be disabled.
[03:37] Marcus Lee: what about LIVECALLS? sometimes we have real-time chat flows that can't accept cross-region hops.
[03:44] Riley Patel: you can tag routes as region-failstop — it'll reject rather than cross-region. we'll include that in the config examples.
[03:51] Clara Gomez: billing — can we get a blended rate for reserved capacity plus burst? we prefer predictable monthly commit and then a smaller premium for burst hours.
[03:59] Avery Chen: yes we have a blended contract template. we'll send revised pricing tiers that include a burst band (hourly charge) and a reserved base (monthly commit).
[04:08] Marcus Lee: and SLAs? for dedicated pools can you guarantee p95 latency and uptime? we need an SLA clause.
[04:15] Avery Chen: dedicated pools have our standard SLA — 99.95% uptime and latency targets tied to model class. we'll include targets for your model size; for burst addendum we offer best-effort with credits if we miss thresholds.
[04:26] Samir Rao: ok. For the onprem pilot — log ingestion and audit trails: we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and the control-plane events to be visible in our Splunk. Is that supported?
[04:36] Riley Patel: yes we support log forwarding via syslog/S3 forwarding or Splunk HEC; we'll provide examples. audit logs are included on private deployments.
[04:44] Clara Gomez: can you share a sample VPC architecture diagram? we need to validate peering with our infra team.
[04:50] Avery Chen: we'll attach a sample VPC diagram and a checklist for peering and firewall rules.
[04:56] Marcus Lee: one last question — competitors. we ran a bake-off with MajorCloudAI and EdgeServe; their burst pricing looked cheaper but their latency was higher. why pick Redwood here?
[05:07] Avery Chen: the tradeoff is control vs cost. Redwood gives you predictable performance plus observability and a clean onprem pathway — if you need predictable p95 for customer-facing flows, the dedicated route reduces operational risk.
[05:18] Clara Gomez: alright makes sense.
[05:21] Avery Chen: recap — we will: (1) send a contract amendment draft that includes reserved APAC pool + burst band and blended pricing; (2) Riley will run a dedicated pool 1k QPS latency benchmark and share logs; (3) share SOC2/KMS doc and VPC diagram; (4) schedule onprem pilot kickoff for week of April 5th if Nimbus confirms internal approvals.
[05:42] Marcus Lee: yep that's the list. can you target sending the contract by april 1?
[05:47] Avery Chen: yes april 1 for contract draft.
[05:50] Clara Gomez: thanks everyone.
[05:52] Samir Rao: thanks.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: some names or acronyms may be slightly off (e.g., HSM spelled out as 'H S M' in audio). occasional filler words removed in places for clarity.
